A classroom contains 40 students. 18 of them read Al-Akhbar newspaper
items.stem: A classroom contains 40 students. 18 of them read Al-Akhbar newspaper, 15 read Al Ahram news paper and 8 read both newspapers. If a student is selected randomly calculate the probability that the student:
solution: Let the event A be reading Al Akhbar newspaper and the event B reading Al Ahram newspaper. then A ∩ B is the event of reading both newspapers.
A: event A: Read Al Akhbar newspaper then $P(A)=\frac{n(A)}{n(S)}=\frac{18}{40}=\frac{9}{20}$
B: Does not read Al Akhbar is the complementary event of the event A and it is A`. $\therefore P(A')=\frac{\text{number of elements of s set }A'}{n(S)}=\frac{15+7}{40}=\frac{22}{40}=\frac{11}{20}$
C: event B: read Al Ahram newspaper then: $P(B)=\frac{n(B)}{n(S)}=\frac{15}{40}=\frac{3}{8}$
D: event A ∩ B means reading both newspaper. $\therefore P(A\cap B)=\frac{n(A\cap B)}{n(S)}=\frac{8}{40}=\frac{1}{5}$
items.notes: Venn diagram k4 is part of the solution. The printed Venn labels and values may conflict with the text (see k4). Part B printed 15+7 as set A' count.

learning_objectives.label: Complementary event and its probability
learning_objectives.description: Determine the complementary event A` of an event A in a sample space S (A ∪ A` = S, A ∩ A` = φ) and calculate P(A`) using P(A`) = 1 - P(A).

learning_objectives.label: Difference between two events
learning_objectives.description: Calculate the probability of the difference between two events, A - B (the occurrence of A only), from set counts or a Venn diagram, using (A - B) ∪ (A ∩ B) = A.
